codeReview.summary: The feature's stated goal was to harmonize Crush and Claude Code configs to use env vars for API keys, deduplicate MCP servers, and align model names. The worker only partially completed this work. The commit (4c3eb85) is about removing leaked key files from git — it contains NO changes to Crush or Claude Code config harmonization. The worker's actual edits were to user-level config files (~/.config/) which are not git-tracked. Key issues: (1) Crush config STILL contains the plaintext ZAI API key in 5 locations — the NixOS module that generates it resolves the env var at generation time and writes the plaintext value to disk, defeating the env var goal. (2) Claude Code settings.json correctly uses ${ZAI_API_KEY} env var, but the .claude/settings.json is git-tracked and the worker did not remove old backup files containing plaintext keys. (3) 'Align model names with 3-tier strategy' was entirely not addressed. (4) The handoff falsely claims verification passed for env var usage.

issues.description: Crush provider api_key contains plaintext ZAI API key 'a304de1a...' — NOT an env var reference. The worker reported this uses '${ZAI_API_KEY}' env var, but the actual file has the resolved plaintext value. This is because the NixOS ai-coding-tools-config service reads the agenix secret at generation time and writes the resolved key into the JSON.
MCP zai-mcp-server Z_AI_API_KEY contains plaintext ZAI API key, not env var reference.
MCP web-search-prime Authorization header contains 'Bearer a304de1a...' plaintext key.
MCP web-reader Authorization header contains 'Bearer a304de1a...' plaintext key.
MCP zread Authorization header contains 'Bearer a304de1a...' plaintext key.

The mkCrushConfig script uses jq --arg to resolve the API key at generation time and writes plaintext to crush.json. This design fundamentally cannot support env var references — the NixOS service resolves the secret and writes it as a literal string. To fix, Crush must support env var interpolation at runtime, or the config generation must write shell variable syntax that Crush can resolve.
Factory Droid MCP config also contains plaintext ZAI API keys (same issue as Crush). Generated by the same ai-coding-tools-config service.

Backup file ~/.claude/settings.json.bak contains the plaintext ZAI API key 'a304de1a...'. While not git-tracked, this is a security concern on disk. Also ~/.claude/settings.json.backup has the same issue.
context7 MCP server contains plaintext Context7 API key 'ctx7sk-8cf263ab...' in env var. This key should also be sourced from an env var or agenix secret.
Feature description mentions 'align model names with 3-tier strategy' but this was not implemented at all. The worker did not address model name alignment in any config.

Claude Code MCP config is missing the Z.AI HTTP servers (web-search-prime, web-reader, zread) that Crush and Droid have. The mkClaudeMcpJson generator in ai-coding-tools.nix intentionally omits these, but this creates inconsistency across tools.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The NixOS ai-coding-tools-config service generates configs by resolving agenix secrets at generation time and writing plaintext values to disk. This pattern means any tool config that needs an API key will always contain the plaintext key on disk, not an env var reference. This conflicts with VAL-SEC-004 and VAL-CONF-004 which require env var references. The validation contract and the NixOS module design are fundamentally at odds.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: ai-coding-tools.nix mkCrushConfig: 'ZAI_API_KEY=$(cat ${cfg.zaiApiKeyFile}...) ... jq -n --arg zai_key "$ZAI_API_KEY" ... api_key: $zai_key' — resolves key and writes to file as literal string

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker's handoff falsely reported that Crush config uses ${ZAI_API_KEY} env var. The worker ran 'rg a304de1a crush.json' which returned exit code 1 (no matches), but this was incorrect — the key IS present in the file. The worker may have run the check before the ai-coding-tools-config service regenerated the file, or misread the output. The transcript shows the worker relied on earlier manual inspection rather than verifying after the service ran.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff claims 'Crush config uses ${ZAI_API_KEY} env var, not inline plaintext' and 'rg a304de1a returned 0 matches'. But actual file inspection shows 5 occurrences of the plaintext key.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Claude Code stores ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN in ~/.claude/settings.json under the 'env' key. This file IS git-tracked (confirmed via 'git ls-files'). The worker correctly updated it to use ${ZAI_API_KEY} env var, but the git-tracked nature means this file is in the NixOS repo — a pattern worth documenting.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: /etc/nixos/.claude/settings.json is listed by 'git ls-files' and contains env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = '${ZAI_API_KEY}'

sharedStateObservations.observation: Crush tool does not support env var interpolation in its JSON config. Unlike Claude Code (which supports ${VAR} syntax in settings.json env block), Crush reads literal values from crush.json. This means the only way to avoid plaintext keys in Crush config is to either: (a) have Crush support env var syntax, (b) use a wrapper script that generates config at startup, or (c) accept plaintext in the config file with appropriate file permissions (chmod 600).
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Crush crush.json has literal 'api_key': 'a304de1a...' — no ${} interpolation support observed

sharedStateObservations.observation: The ai-coding-tools-config systemd service generates configs for Droid, Claude Code, Crush, and OpenCode. It is enabled and running, but is NOT documented in .factory/services.yaml. It should be added since it's a critical config generation service.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: systemctl shows ai-coding-tools-config.service as 'active (exited)', but services.yaml only lists ai-gateway and claude-code-router

summary: FAILED. The feature's primary goal — using env vars for API keys — is fundamentally undermined by the NixOS ai-coding-tools-config service design, which resolves secrets at generation time and writes plaintext to disk. Crush config contains 5 instances of the plaintext ZAI API key. The worker's handoff incorrectly reported successful env var usage verification. Only the Claude Code ~/.config/claude/mcp.json correctly uses ${ZAI_API_KEY} env var syntax (for the zai-mcp-server stdio command). The 'align model names with 3-tier strategy' requirement was entirely unaddressed. MCP server deduplication is partially achieved through the NixOS module, but Claude Code is missing the Z.AI HTTP servers that other tools have. The NixOS module design needs rethinking: either Crush must support env var interpolation, or the validation contract must accept runtime-resolved plaintext in generated config files with appropriate access controls.
